summary: I focused on the seams between Graph SDK authentication, aiohttp/thread event loops, scheduler persistence, tenant storage, navigator-auth backend registration, and source-schema introspection. The largest risks are an incomplete scheduler persistence path, accidental reuse of corporate Azure authentication, and making a link-only provider participate in normal login dispatch.

suggestions.title: Add a first-class link-only backend contract
suggestions.rationale: `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` currently contains only `BasicAuth`, while `ExternalAuth.configure()` registers login, callback, logout, and credential-check routes, and the auth middleware iterates every configured backend. Adding `OneDriveAuth` without a link-only registration mechanism can expose it as a login method and make unauthenticated requests probe it. Prefer navigator-auth support for identity-only backends, or explicitly override route registration and authentication dispatch with tests proving only identity-link routes exist.

suggestions.title: Remove the ambiguous Azure provider fallback
suggestions.rationale: The proposed `provider: azure` option conflicts with the stated isolation requirement: the installed `AzureAuth` uses corporate tenant configuration and a global `AZURE_IDENTITY_SCOPES`, while the identity handlers refresh through whichever backend is named by the stored provider. A delegated OneDrive source should accept only `onedrive` identities, with an explicit mode matrix (`app_only` versus `delegated`) that rejects incompatible `user`, secret, and path combinations.

suggestions.title: Introduce an explicit pre-thread credential phase and token adapter
suggestions.rationale: `ThreadSource.run()` creates a fresh event loop, whereas vault access is asynchronous and uses database/Redis resources owned by the request loop. Also, the installed `GraphServiceClient` accepts a `TokenCredential` or `AsyncTokenCredential`, not a raw access-token string. Add a no-op async preparation hook on `ThreadSource`, invoke it from `MultiQS` before `start()`, and pass only a short-lived credential context into the worker; use an `AsyncTokenCredential` adapter whose `get_token()` returns the resolved `AccessToken`. Do not access `SessionVault` from `fetch()`.

suggestions.title: Inject scheduler auth context instead of relying on request state
suggestions.rationale: `scheduled_multiqs_job()` currently constructs `MultiQS(slug=slug, tenant=tenant)` and ignores extra keyword arguments. `QSScheduler` also does not retain the application/auth handler, so a scheduled delegated source has no path to `authdb`, the OneDrive backend, or the stored `run_as_user_id`. Pass an explicit resolver service or scheduler-owned app context on the scheduler loop, and keep only the user ID and non-secret ownership metadata in APScheduler job kwargs.

suggestions.title: Extend the complete persistence boundary and tolerate old schemas
suggestions.rationale: Adding the field only to `QueryModel` is insufficient: tenant stores use the separate `TenantQueryDefinition`, and the scheduler repository hard-codes `_SCHEDULABLE_COLUMNS`. Selecting `scheduler_run_as_user_id` unconditionally will make `schedulable()` fail for every un-migrated store rather than return `NULL`. Add the field to both models, include it in repository row handling, and select `NULL AS scheduler_run_as_user_id` when a store lacks the column; update tenant fixtures and DDL gates accordingly.

suggestions.title: Assign run-as ownership in the definition transaction, not scheduler sync
suggestions.rationale: `SchedulerJobsView.post()` only synchronizes an already-persisted row; it is not the definition write path. Actual mutations occur in `QueryManager` and `DefinitionRepository`, which currently commit before scheduler synchronization. If the scheduler endpoint assigns the current user, any caller able to resync a slug can silently reassign its delegated identity; if ordinary definition edits overwrite the field, unrelated edits also change ownership. Capture the authenticated numeric user only when a schedule is created or explicitly changed, reject the field from request payloads, preserve it on ordinary edits, and write the audit row in the same repository transaction.

suggestions.title: Make audit immutability enforceable by the database
suggestions.rationale: An `INSERT`/`SELECT` grant does not guarantee append-only behavior when the application role owns the table or has inherited privileges. Define whether the audit table is per tenant schema or centralized, use a separate owner role plus restricted application grants, and add a database trigger or equivalent protection against `UPDATE` and `DELETE`. Add rollout tests for both public and tenant stores.

suggestions.title: Test the Graph contract and preserve SharePoint behavior explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `tests/test_source_sharepoint.py` currently covers construction, parsing, and missing imports, but not Graph request-builder paths, `/shares` resolution, download URL retrieval, credential closure, timeout, or drive fallback. `tests/test_source_registry.py` also asserts exactly five sources, so registration will require a deliberate test update. Add mocked Graph tests for Business app-only, delegated `/me`, personal sharing URLs, invalid mode combinations, and SharePoint directory normalization; keep the existing SharePoint tests unchanged where possible and add schema/registry assertions separately.

suggestions.title: Avoid leaking a process-wide platform.version patch
suggestions.rationale: The existing SharePoint fetch replaces `platform.version` globally and never restores it. Extracting that code into a shared base increases concurrent app-only/delegated fetches and makes the mutation affect unrelated SDK calls. Wrap the patch in a narrowly scoped context that restores the original function in `finally`, and close only credentials created by the base; the static delegated token adapter should not be treated as an async Azure credential requiring closure.

suggestions.title: Keep introspection-visible field access or add an explicit catalog
suggestions.rationale: `extract_source_schema()` discovers fields by regex over `__init__` bodies and walks the MRO; it will not see credential or source fields hidden behind helper methods. Moving common parsing into a helper can silently omit `auth`, `provider`, `user`, or delegated path fields from generated documentation. Either retain literal `options.get(...)`/aliased-container access in the inspected constructors or add a companion catalog, then assert the generated SharePoint schema is unchanged and the OneDrive schema contains every mode field.
